items.title: Intel Is Said to Near Share Sale Upsize to Raise $20 Billion
items.author: Bailey Lipschultz, Ryan Gould and Ian King
items.content: <article>Intel Corp. is seeking to increase the amount it’s raising in a share sale to about $20 billion, according to people familiar with the matter, a third more than it was targeting when it announced the deal Monday morning.</article>

items.title: Asian Bank Stocks Rally as Investors Seek Safety From Volatile AI Trade
items.author: Winnie Hsu
items.content: <article>Asian banks are staging one of their strongest stock rallies in decades, a trend that may continue as investors look for a safer bet in the face of the volatile AI trade.</article>

items.title: Google’s AI Team Tells Job Seekers Its HR Filters Are Unreliable
items.author: Julia Love
items.content: <article>Alphabet Inc.’s Google pitches its artificial intelligence tools to corporate clients as a way to more quickly sift through a mountain of job applications to find the most promising candidates. Some of its own AI researchers don’t want to rely on these tools when recruiting.</article>

items.title: Trump Media Losses Hit $238 Million as Firm Pivots to Fast Feeds
items.author: Annie Massa
items.content: <article>Donald Trump’s social media company posted steeper losses as it careened from a big cryptocurrency bet into a controversial new line of business selling faster access to market-moving posts from the US president.</article>

items.title: Five Takeaways From Zuckerberg's 6,500-word Manifesto on AI
items.content: <article>Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg touted his views on artificial intelligence in a 6,500-word essay published Monday, emphasizing his belief that wider access to AI models is key to the industry’s future. Rileyr Griffin has the five key takeaways.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Five Takeaways From Zuckerberg’s 6,500-Word Manifesto on AI
items.author: Riley Griffin and Kurt Wagner
items.content: <article>Meta Platforms Inc. Chief Executive Officer Mark Zuckerberg touted his views on artificial intelligence in a 6,500-word essay published Monday, emphasizing his belief that wider access to AI models is key to the industry’s future.</article>

items.title: Webtoon Buys $100 Million Share in Game Studio to Expand Reach
items.author: Sohee Kim
items.content: <article>Webtoon Entertainment Inc. is buying a majority stake in a Korean gaming studio for about $100 million, in its latest push to expand a content portfolio that includes web comics, anime and gaming.</article>

items.title: OpenAI Buys Back $7 Billion of Employee Shares in Tender Offer
items.author: Rebecca Torrence and Shirin Ghaffary
items.content: <article>OpenAI has completed a deal to help employees sell roughly $7 billion worth of shares in the company ahead of a possible Wall Street debut, according to a person familiar with the matter.</article>

items.title: Bart Scott on Jets’ Partnership With Outfront
items.content: <article>Former NY Jets Linebacker Bart Scott sat down with Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick to discuss the Jets new advertising partnership with Outfront Media, the state of sports media, and Scott's future plans in the media industry. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Investor ETF Appeal Of Photonics
items.content: <article>Mayuranki De, vice president of ETF Trade Strategy at Raymond James, joins Isabelle Lee and Eric Balchunas on "Bloomberg ETF IQ." They discuss the Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF (ticker: LYTE), an actively managed ETF that seeks to provide capital appreciation. The Fund invests in the equity securities of companies whose core technology involves generating, manipulating, detecting, or transmitting light for various technologies, such as AI data centers, defense, medical imaging, industrial manufacturing, and quantum computing. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: OpenAI Is Hiring a Power-Trading Lead for Its Data Center Portfolio
items.author: Julian Hast
items.content: <article>OpenAI is hiring a power-trading lead to help manage the expanding energy needs of the electricity-intensive data centers running its artificial intelligence models.</article>

items.title: 'Overwhelming Demand' for Crypto ETFs: Mitchnick
items.content: <article>Robert Mitchnick, head of digital assets at BlackRock, joins Isabelle Lee and Eric Balchunas on "Bloomberg ETF IQ." Hackers have stolen more than $130 million worth of Bitcoin from thousands of supposedly secure cold wallets in recent days. The Coldcard wallet hack may strengthen the case for spot Bitcoin ETFs by undermining confidence in self-custody among investors. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: ETFs Offer 'Trusted Vehicle' for Bitcoin: Mitchnick
items.content: <article>Robert Mitchnick, head of digital assets at BlackRock, joins Isabelle Lee and Eric Balchunas on "Bloomberg ETF IQ." Hackers have stolen more than $130 million worth of Bitcoin from thousands of supposedly secure cold wallets in recent days. The Coldcard wallet hack may strengthen the case for spot Bitcoin ETFs by undermining confidence in self-custody among investors. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Meta Brings Powerful AI to the Personal Computer
items.content: <article>Meta is escalating the debate over open versus closed AI with Muse Glimmer, a new downloadable model designed to run on a personal computer using a single GPU. The release, accompanied by a new essay from CEO Mark Zuckerberg, underscores Meta's push for more accessible and customizable AI as low-cost open models from China intensify pressure on rivals including OpenAI and Anthropic. Bloomberg's Kurt Wagner joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: South Park Commons Raises Ambitions for the AI Era
items.content: <article>South Park Commons is expanding its investment strategy as AI pushes founders toward increasingly ambitious and capital-intensive ideas. Co-founder and General Partner Aditya Agarwal joins Bloomberg to discuss the firm’s “minus one to zero” approach to backing entrepreneurs before their ideas fully take shape, why its new fund will allow it to write bigger checks and invest for longer, and how early bets on founders like Cognition CEO Scott Wu are shaping its strategy. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: From Coding to Finance: Microsoft’s AI Agent Push
items.content: <article>Microsoft says AI agents are already fundamentally changing how its software engineers work — and sales, finance and other knowledge workers are next. Charles Lamanna, Microsoft EVP of Copilot, Agents and Platform, joins Bloomberg to explain how employees are shifting from doing tasks themselves to overseeing AI agents, why the company sees the technology driving more productivity rather than simply reducing headcount, and what’s behind Microsoft 365 Copilot’s surge past 30 million paid seats. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: GameStop Rethinks Its eBay Play
items.content: <article>GameStop is considering dropping its bid for eBay and pursuing a partnership instead, according to sources. Bloomberg’s Bailey Lipschultz and Spencer Soper explain how GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen could seek to leverage its 1,600 US stores to give eBay a physical retail presence - and why a partnership may prove more realistic than an outright deal. They join Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Baillie Gifford’s McPadden Backs TSMC, SK Hynix Over China Chips
items.author: Ed Ludlow
items.content: <article>Baillie Gifford & Co.’s Paulina McPadden said companies like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. and SK Hynix Inc. hold near-monopoly positions in advanced chip manufacturing that China will struggle to match, even as Beijing mobilizes its stock and bond market to fund its AI ambitions.</article>

items.title: Nvidia Taps Wall Street for $500 Billion Funding Commitment
items.author: Silla Brush, Ian King and Todd Gillespie
items.content: <article>US investment giants including Apollo Global Management Inc., Blackstone Inc., BlackRock Inc. and Brookfield Asset Management are partnering with Nvidia Corp. to invest $500 billion in artificial intelligence infrastructure.</article>

items.title: Intel to Sell $15 Billion in Stock After AI Boosts Demand
items.author: Ian King
items.content: <article>Intel Corp. is offering $15 billion worth of new stock in what represents its first public share sale since the chipmaker listed in 1971, a bid to extend its comeback and capitalize on the AI boom.</article>
